questions.stem: Standing in the boat and facing the bow, which side is on your right?
questions.explanation: Facing forward, starboard is the right side and port is the left.

questions.stem: What is the freeboard of a boat?
questions.explanation: Freeboard is the height of the hull above the water. Depth below is draught and the widest part is the beam.

questions.stem: Where on a boat is the compliance notice (capacity plate) normally found?
questions.explanation: It is fixed near the helm where the operator can see it.

questions.stem: A 5 m runabout's compliance notice gives a maximum number of people and a maximum weight. When is the boat full?
questions.explanation: The boat is at capacity at the people limit or the weight limit, whichever comes first.

questions.stem: Which of these does the compliance notice on a 5 m outboard boat show?
options: The fuel tank capacity in litres
The top speed at full throttle
The hull serial number of the boat
questions.explanation: On boats up to 6 m the notice shows recommended maximum people, weight and outboard power.

questions.stem: The capacity limits on your boat's compliance notice assume what conditions?
questions.explanation: The limits are for good weather with the weight spread evenly. Carry less when it is rough.

questions.stem: Where is the hull serial number marked on a pleasure craft?
options: Lower port corner of the transom
Starboard side of the bow, inside
On the console under the helm
questions.explanation: The HIN is marked on the outside upper starboard corner of the transom, or as close to it as possible.

questions.stem: How many characters does a hull serial number have?
questions.explanation: The hull serial number has 12 characters.

questions.stem: You are loading camping gear into a small open boat. What is the best way?
options: Stack it high on the seats
All in the bow to lift the stern
All on the side opposite you
questions.explanation: Weight kept low, spread evenly and secured keeps the boat stable.

questions.stem: Your open boat has filled with water but is still upright. What has happened?
questions.explanation: Swamped means full of water but upright. Capsized means turned over.

questions.stem: Why does overloading make a small boat more likely to take on water?
questions.explanation: More weight pushes the boat lower, so there is less freeboard and small waves can come aboard.

questions.stem: A friend wants to move from the stern seat to the bow of a small aluminum boat while you fish. What should they do?
options: Stay low and near the centre
questions.explanation: Keep the centre of gravity low and central when moving in a small boat.

questions.stem: Which kind of hull rises up and skims across the water at speed?
questions.explanation: A planing hull lifts and skims at speed. A displacement hull pushes the water aside and is speed-limited.
